name: Latvia
headline: Latvia: +2.1% growth in 2025, 3.8% inflation, debt 47% of GDP
sections: Latvia is a $48.6 billion economy (2025), the world's 101st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.1% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $46K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 10.0% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 3.8% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 17.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 6.9% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 12.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 47% of GDP (2025), a moderate level. The general government balance is −4.0% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −5.3% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 130% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.8% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 55% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 76.4 years (2024). Population: 1.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
